_: FITLOG_SLEEP_P1. Against the reconstructed previous build there is no
health_sleep_blocks table and no sleep_night(), and two blocks of one
night collide on hae|sleep_hours|day|<date>|00:00:00 so the second
replaces the first -- which is the truncation this phase exists to stop.
Three assertions guard properties the previous build ALSO satisfied, or
would have failed against for a trivial reason (the function simply did
not exist) rather than because the property was violated. Those are put
under mutation control instead, which is the stronger evidence: it shows
the assertion responds to the thing it claims to measure.
M_awake   -- count awake time as sleep. Assertion 09 must catch it.
M_overlap -- stop clustering overlapping blocks, so a night that is
re-segmented by a later export is added to itself.
M_wakedate-- file a block by the day it STARTED rather than the wake
date Auto Export gives it, which splits every night that
crosses midnight across two days. Assertion 07 must

assertions.name: 01 a 5h41m night delivered in two blocks
04 replaying the night does not add it to itself
06 blocks arriving in separate payloads combine
08 asleep=0 beside real stages is not a zero night
10 a UTC-stamped block is stored in IST
05 a re-segmented night is not added to itself

mutation.why: overlapping blocks stop being clustered, so a night re-sent as one merged block is added to the two it replaces
mutation.replace: if False and clusters and b["start_ts"] < clusters[-1]["end"]:

assertions.name: 07 a night that starts before midnight is filed under its wake

mutation.why: a block is filed by the day it started instead of the wake date Auto Export gives it, splitting every cross-midnight night in two

assertions.name: 09 awake time is never counted as sleep

mutation.why: awake time is added to the asleep total, which is the classic way a sleep record overstates a broken night
